records.name: El Pasoans Fighting Hunger Food Bank
records.description_en: The regional food bank for El Paso. It supplies food pantries and food programs across the area and can help you find food near you.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the El Paso area who need food.
records.how_to_apply: Call the food bank to find food distributions or a partner pantry near you.
records.notes: Phone confirmed on City of El Paso Community & Homeless Assistance page. The food bank's own site (epfh.org) could not be loaded this session, so address and hours were not confirmed. Also listed as a Feeding America member food bank.

records.name: Kelly Center for Hunger Relief Food Pantry
records.description_en: A food pantry that gives emergency and extra food to El Pasoans in need. It also has a clothes closet and a self-sufficiency program called FreshStart.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso residents who need food. Call to ask about requirements.
records.how_to_apply: Call or email the Kelly Center to ask about pantry days and what to bring.
records.notes: Email: Info@KellyFresh.org. Street address is from the City of El Paso 'El Paso Helps' food page (elpasohelps.org/food); the org site did not list it.

records.name: The Salvation Army of El Paso - Shelter, Meals and Emergency Assistance
records.organization: The Salvation Army of El Paso
records.description_en: Provides emergency shelter, meals, and emergency financial help. It may help with rent, mortgage, or utility bills based on need.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in El Paso facing hardship or homelessness. Help with bills depends on need and available funds.
records.how_to_apply: Call the main office or visit 4300 E. Paisano Dr. to ask about shelter, meals, or bill help.
records.notes: El Paso Helps lists (915) 521-7229 for shelter & food. El Paso Water lists Salvation Army for rental, mortgage, and utility assistance based on need. Citadel Corps: 4900 Hercules Ave, (915) 755-4168.

records.name: El Paso County Nutrition Program (Senior Meals)
records.description_en: Noon meals for seniors at senior and community centers across El Paso County. Homebound adults may get meals delivered to their home.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults age 60 and older. Home delivery is for homebound people referred by Texas HHS.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 273-3498 to join congregate meals. For home-delivered meals, call HHS Community Care Services at 1-855-710-3237 for a referral.
records.hours: Centers open Monday - Friday, 9 am to 4 pm
records.notes: Sites include city centers (Carolina, Eastside, Pavo Real, Grandview, Hilos de Plata, Memorial, Southside, Wellington Chew, Polly Harris, San Juan), county centers (Canutillo, San Elizario, Clint, Fabens), and partners (Montana Vista/La Fe, Socorro). Cost not stated on page.

records.name: City of El Paso WIC (Women, Infants, and Children)
records.organization: City of El Paso Department of Public Health
records.description_en: WIC gives healthy food benefits on a WIC card, nutrition classes, and breastfeeding support. It also gives referrals to health and social services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant women, new moms, infants, and children under 5 who meet WIC income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Start your application online or by phone at 915-212-4WIC (4942). You will then have an appointment to confirm eligibility.
records.notes: Clinic hours are posted as location-specific PDFs on the city page. Texas WIC Breastfeeding Hotline: 855-550-6667 (24/7).

records.name: La Fe WIC Program
records.organization: Centro de Salud Familiar La Fe
records.description_en: WIC offices that give nutrition help, food benefits, and breastfeeding support. Staff are bilingual.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income pregnant women, new moms, infants, and young children in El Paso County who qualify for WIC.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the Yandell or Ochoa WIC office.
records.hours: 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. Friday
records.notes: Second office: Ochoa WIC, 700 S. Ochoa, El Paso, TX 79901, (915) 545-7048, same hours. Page says staff are bilingual; Spanish assumed as the second language.

records.name: Project BRAVO Utility Assistance (CEAP/LIHEAP)
records.organization: Project BRAVO (El Paso Community Action Program)
records.description_en: Helps pay gas, electric, and propane bills for low-income households. Project BRAVO also runs weatherization, HVAC repair, and housing programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income El Paso County households who need help with energy bills. Payment amounts depend on federal funding, usage, and household size.
records.how_to_apply: Apply in person at one of the four Project BRAVO centers. Applications are not accepted online. Help can take 4-6 weeks after your application is complete.
records.notes: Centers: Central 2000 Texas Ave 79901 (ext 117); Northeast/Westside 4838 Montana 79903 (ext 342); Eastside 14901 Whitetail Deer Dr 79938 (ext 350); Ysleta 8908 Old County Rd 79907 (ext 300). All via (915) 562-4100. Email contact@projectbravo.org. Site says application window opened July 1 at 8 AM. Also the El Paso agency for Texas Gas Service 'Share The Warmth'.

records.name: Share The Warmth (Texas Gas Service) - El Paso
records.description_en: Donation-funded help paying home heating (gas) bills for Texas Gas Service customers in an emergency. In El Paso, you apply through Project BRAVO.
records.eligibility_summary_en: You must pay your home heating bill, live in a Texas Gas Service county, and face an immediate money emergency.
records.how_to_apply: Apply at Project BRAVO in El Paso.
records.notes: Phone is Project BRAVO's main line (confirmed at projectbravo.org/contact). Texas Gas Service customer service: 800-700-2443.

records.name: AguaCares Water Bill Assistance
records.description_en: Gives up to a $250 credit per year on your El Paso Water bill if you are at risk of having your water shut off.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso Water customers facing money hardship and at risk of disconnection. You must agree to a payment plan for any past-due balance. Once per year.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online with the required documents during an open application period. Funds open monthly and can run out.
records.notes: As of this research, September funds were exhausted and the next period opens October 1, 2026. Related: AguaRepairs leak repair for homeowners, run by Rebuilding Together El Paso, (915) 832-7010.

records.name: Bright Hearts Fund and Payment Arrangements
records.description_en: Donation-funded help for El Paso Electric customers who are behind and at risk of disconnection. EPE also offers payment arrangements and budget billing.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso Electric customers who are past due and at risk of having power shut off.
records.how_to_apply: Contact El Paso Electric and ask about assistance programs, the Bright Hearts Fund, or a payment arrangement.
records.notes: EPE serves El Paso and parts of New Mexico. Texas customers may also qualify for low-income rider programs. Phone not confirmed this session.

records.name: Senior and Disabled Discount on Environmental Services Fee
records.organization: City of El Paso Environmental Services
records.description_en: Gives a discount on the monthly trash (solid waste) fee on your water bill.
records.eligibility_summary_en: You must be the main water account holder and be 65 or older, or be 100 percent disabled as certified by Social Security, the VA, or a public disability pension.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: City of El Paso water account holder

records.how_to_apply: Apply online or mail the Senior/Disability Discount form. This discount cannot be combined with side-door collection.
records.notes: People under 65 qualify if 100% disabled (disability path).

records.name: El Paso County General Assistance (Emergency Rent, Mortgage and Utility Aid)
records.description_en: Helps El Paso County residents with emergency rent or mortgage payments and emergency utility bills. It also runs the county burial assistance program.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso County residents only. Income limits apply based on family size. Help depends on grant funding.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online or call General Assistance at 915-273-3496.
records.hours: Monday through Friday 8 am to 5 pm
records.notes: Income limits are in the 'Income Guidelines by Family Size 2025' PDF on the county page. Community Services main line (915) 273-3485; email Communitysvcs@epcounty.com. Hours are from the Community Services page.

records.name: Center for Resiliency - Rental and Utility Assistance (El Paso United)
records.organization: United Way of El Paso County
records.description_en: Helps with short- to medium-term rent paid to landlords, utility payments to stop shutoffs, and up to three months of back rent to prevent eviction. Also offers counseling and support groups.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso households at risk of losing housing who meet HUD program rules. Staff screen you at intake.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 400-7401 or visit the Center for Resiliency for intake and screening.
records.notes: Funded by HOME-ARP. Located at the Family Youth Services Center. City of El Paso also refers rent/utility help here and to the El Paso Helps portal.

records.name: Amistad for Veterans Project - General Assistance
records.description_en: Helps veterans and their families pay rent, mortgage, rental deposits, utility bills, and internet bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For veterans and their families in the El Paso area.
records.how_to_apply: Call 915-298-7307 and select Option 1, then Option 1, then enter your zip code.
records.notes: Funded by the Texas Veterans Commission Fund for Veterans Assistance. City of El Paso lists (915) 298-1107 for this program.

records.name: Amistad Street Outreach Program
records.description_en: Outreach workers help people living on the street connect to shelter, housing, and services. They give hygiene kits, referrals, and rides to a shelter when asked.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people sleeping on the street or in places not meant for living.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 532-3790 Option 4, or the 24/7 line (915) 298-1115 for a homeless person in need.
records.notes: 24/7 number (915) 298-1115 is also the El Paso Helps homeless hotline. Address from elpasohelps.org/housing.

records.name: Opportunity Center for the Homeless (Welcome Center and Shelters)
records.description_en: Runs emergency shelters for men, women, families, seniors, and veterans. The Welcome Center offers shelter, meals, showers, laundry, and case management.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone experiencing homelessness, regardless of mental health, substance use, or other challenges.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the Welcome Center at 201 East 9th Ave. or call (915) 248-5567.
records.hours: Welcome Center: M-F 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
records.notes: Main office (915) 577-0069, ocinfo@ocelpaso.org. Sites include Men's and Women's Resource Centers, WSR Family Center, La Casa de Las Abuelitas, Magoffin SRO, and Magoffin Veterans Shelter. Welcome Center address/hours/phone from City of El Paso El Paso Helps shelter page.

records.name: Rescue Mission of El Paso Shelter
records.description_en: Shelter with free meals for people experiencing homelessness. It also has programs for people recovering from addiction.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people experiencing homelessness. Call to ask about intake.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit 221 North Lee St. to ask about intake.
records.notes: Email info@rmelp.org. Intake hours not listed.

records.name: Annunciation House
records.description_en: Offers shelter and hospitality to migrants, immigrants, and refugees in El Paso.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For migrants, refugees, and very poor people of the border who often cannot get help from other agencies.
records.how_to_apply: Call Annunciation House to ask about space.
records.notes: Org site confirms mission; address and phone are from the City of El Paso 'El Paso Helps' shelter page (elpasohelps.org/shelter).

records.name: Center Against Sexual and Family Violence (CASFV)
records.organization: Center Against Sexual and Family Violence
records.description_en: 24/7 hotline, emergency shelter, and transitional housing for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault. Also offers counseling, legal advocacy, and financial skills programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For survivors of domestic violence or sexual assault and their families in El Paso, Hudspeth, and Culberson counties.
records.hours: Hotline 24/7. Family Resource Center: Monday-Thursday 8 a.m.-6 p.m., Friday 8 a.m.-noon
records.notes: Also serves Hudspeth and Culberson counties. Toll-free 1-800-727-0511. Shelter location is confidential; 580 Giles Road is the listed organization address.

records.name: Child Crisis Center of El Paso - Emergency Shelter and Respite Care
records.organization: Child Crisis Center of El Paso
records.description_en: Emergency shelter for children and respite care for families in crisis.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For children and families in crisis in El Paso. Call to ask about eligibility.
records.notes: El Paso Helps lists (915) 562-4673 as another number.

records.name: YWCA El Paso del Norte Region - Housing and Child Care
records.organization: YWCA El Paso del Norte Region
records.description_en: Offers a housing assistance program, after-school and camp programs for kids, and adult education and literacy classes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso families and individuals. Call for program-specific rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call 915-519-0000 or email info@ywcaelpaso.org.

records.name: HOME - Housing Choice Vouchers and Affordable Communities
records.organization: Housing Opportunity Management Enterprises (HOME), formerly Housing Authority of the City of El Paso
records.description_en: Runs the Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) program and affordable housing communities in El Paso. It also has a Family Self-Sufficiency program with job coaching and savings.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income families who meet federal housing program rules. Call or apply online to check waitlists.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Applicant Portal on the HOME website, book an appointment online, or call for an appointment.
records.notes: hacep.org redirects to ephome.org. Waitlist status not shown.

records.name: Sun Metro Reduced Fare ID
records.description_en: A free ID card that lets you ride Sun Metro buses at a lower fare.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people 65 and older, people with disabilities, Medicare card holders, students, and active duty military, retirees, and their dependents.
documents_needed: Government photo ID showing date of birth (seniors)
records.how_to_apply: Bring your documents to a Sun Metro ticket office to get your Reduced Fare ID.
records.notes: Social Security letters are not accepted as disability proof. Disability ID valid 5 years (permanent) or up to 12 months (temporary). Seniors may also use a valid Enhanced Library Card. Fare amounts not listed on page.

records.name: Sun Metro LIFT Paratransit
records.description_en: Door-to-door shared rides for people whose disability keeps them from using regular city buses.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people with a disability that prevents them from getting to a bus stop or riding a regular bus on their own. Visitors can ride up to 21 days a year.
documents_needed: Paratransit Verification Form completed by a doctor or LIFT representative
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the LIFT application online or on paper, and have a doctor complete the verification form. Submit by email, mail, or in person.
records.notes: Phone shown as 915.212.LIFT (5438). Permanent eligibility recertified every 3 years. Printable forms in English and Spanish.

records.name: Sun Metro Vets Ride Free
records.description_en: Free 30-day bus passes for fixed route, Brio, and LIFT rides for veterans, their dependents, and surviving spouses.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For veterans, eligible dependents, and surviving spouses, while grant funds last.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Texas Veterans form online or call 915-212-3333. Past participants can call to confirm their information.
records.notes: Grant runs September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 or until funds run out, first come first served. Funded by Texas Veterans Commission.

records.name: Amistad Transportation Services
records.description_en: Rides to medical visits, cancer treatment, dialysis, therapy, and pharmacies for eligible people, plus mobility help for seniors and people with disabilities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For eligible Medicaid clients, Children with Special Health Care Needs, and people in the Transportation for Indigent Cancer Patients program, plus seniors and people with disabilities.
records.how_to_apply: If you have a Medicaid health plan, contact your plan to schedule rides. Otherwise call Amistad at (915) 532-3415.
records.notes: Page also lists 877-633-8747 for non-Medicaid trip scheduling and notes the Medicaid MTO program moved to Access2Care in 2021; details may be outdated, so call first. Serves Far West Texas including Big Bend area.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Borderplex Career Centers
records.description_en: Free job search help, career counseling, resumes, and job training. May help with gas money, interview clothes, and child care scholarships. Runs SNAP and TANF work programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For job seekers in El Paso and nearby counties. Some services are for qualified job seekers only.
records.how_to_apply: Create a free career profile on WorkInTexas.com, or visit a Workforce Solutions center.
records.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM
records.notes: Other El Paso sites: Northeast Center 8941 Dyer St. 79904 (same hours); Military Affiliated Satellite, Bldg 725 Custer Rd, Fort Bliss 79906 (M-F 7:30-4); Main Library 501 N. Oregon, Rm 309, 79901 (M-Th 10-5, F 1-5). Board also serves Brewster, Culberson, Hudspeth, Jeff Davis, Presidio.

records.name: CareForce Child Care Scholarships
records.description_en: Helps working or studying parents pay for child care at approved providers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Parents in the household must work, go to school, or train at least 25 hours a week on average, have primary custody, and earn under 85% of state median income (for example, $6,443 a month for a family of 3).

eligibility_rules.residency_required: El Paso, Brewster, Culberson, Hudspeth, Jeff Davis, or Presidio County

records.how_to_apply: Create an account and complete the pre-screening form online. Upload documents when you are notified.
records.notes: Waitlist is typically 6-12 months or longer. Income limits (85% SMI): family of 2 $5,216/mo; 3 $6,443; 4 $7,670; 5 $8,897.

records.name: Emergence Health Network (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.description_en: The local mental health authority for El Paso. It offers a 24/7 crisis line and services for mental illness, substance use, and developmental disabilities for adults and children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso County residents needing mental health, substance use, or developmental disability services. Crisis help is open to anyone.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis call 915-779-1800 or 988. For services, call Centralized Scheduling at (915) 242-0555.
records.hours: Crisis and emergency services 24 hours, 7 days a week
records.notes: Toll-free crisis: 1-877-562-6467. Crisis services also at 1601 Yandell Dr. Program selection (915) 887-3410. Offers MAT for substance use.

records.name: Centro San Vicente Health Center
records.description_en: Community health center offering primary care, dental, behavioral health, pharmacy, lab, and X-ray services at several El Paso clinics.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone. The center says no patient will be refused services, and financial help programs are available.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 859-7545 to make an appointment.
records.notes: Clinics: Alameda, San Elizario (915) 851-0999, Pebble Hills (915) 773-0606, and at the Opportunity Center (El Paso Helps lists 1208 Myrtle Ave). Toll-free 1-877-415-5106.

records.name: Centro de Salud Familiar La Fe Health Clinics
records.organization: Centro de Salud Familiar La Fe
records.description_en: Community clinics offering adult and child medical care, eye care, and behavioral health. Charges are based on your income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves all patients regardless of ability to pay. Discounts depend on family size and income.
documents_needed: Proof of income (recent paycheck stub or last year's tax return)
Proof of address (utility bill or rent receipt)
Photo ID, birth certificate, or driver's license
Medicare, Medicaid, or insurance card if you have one
records.how_to_apply: Register as a patient at a La Fe clinic. Ask at the front desk to apply for a discount.
records.notes: Seven clinics including Central, Lisbon, Yandell Adult, Jose Roman MD Pediatric, San Elizario, Westway, and Optometry. Staff can help if you lack documents.

records.name: Project Vida Health Center and Community Services
records.description_en: Health clinics, pediatrics, behavioral health, and pharmacy, plus case management, affordable housing, homelessness prevention, and early childhood programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For El Paso residents, especially low-income families. Call for program rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 465-1191 or visit 3607 Rivera Ave.
records.notes: New Maxwell location at 4875 Maxwell Ave. opening Fall 2026.

records.name: UMC El Paso Charity Care Program
records.organization: University Medical Center of El Paso (El Paso County Hospital District)
records.description_en: Free or reduced-cost hospital care at UMC for uninsured or underinsured people with low income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For uninsured or underinsured people whose income is within federal poverty guideline limits set by UMC. You must show residency.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: El Paso County (proof of residency required)

documents_needed: Proof of income (tax return, W-2, last 2 paychecks, unemployment papers, employer letter, or bank statements)
Two proofs of residency (mail, driver's license, school records, property tax, rent, mortgage, or utility receipts)
records.how_to_apply: Contact Patient Financial Services. Staff will help you complete the application.
records.notes: Applications available in English and Spanish. Exact FPL percentage not stated on page. Hospital main line (915) 544-1200.

records.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid - El Paso Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as housing, eviction, and benefits problems.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income people who meet TRLA's eligibility rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call the intake line at (956) 996-8752 or toll-free (833) 329-8752 to apply.
records.hours: 9:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. (Central Time), Monday through Friday
records.notes: Hours listed in Central Time (El Paso is Mountain Time, one hour earlier). TRLA homepage has a bilingual apply message.

records.name: Las Americas Immigrant Advocacy Center
records.description_en: Legal help for low-income immigrants in El Paso.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income immigrants.
records.notes: Fees not stated on site.

records.name: Rio Grande Area Agency on Aging
records.description_en: Helps older adults and caregivers with information and referral, care coordination, benefits counseling, caregiver support, and a nursing home ombudsman.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people age 60 and older and their families.
records.hours: Monday - Thursday 8 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Friday 8 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.
records.notes: Also serves Hudspeth, Culberson, Jeff Davis, Presidio, and Brewster counties. Hours from RIOCOG homepage. Benefits counseling covers Medicare questions.

records.name: El Paso County Veterans Assistance Office
records.description_en: Helps veterans, dependents, and surviving spouses apply for VA benefits, file disability claims and appeals, and connect to local help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For veterans living in El Paso County, and their dependents and surviving spouses.
records.how_to_apply: Call 915-875-8570 to schedule an appointment.
records.hours: East Annex: Monday-Wednesday and Friday, 8am-4pm (closed Thursday)
records.notes: Northeast office: 4641 Cohen Ave Suite D, El Paso, TX 79924, Monday-Friday 8am-4pm.

records.name: 2-1-1 Call Center (City of El Paso Public Health)
records.organization: City of El Paso Department of Public Health
records.description_en: A free 24/7 helpline that connects you to food pantries, housing help, child care, counseling, medical care, and other local services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone in the El Paso area who needs help finding services.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

records.name: HOPWA Housing Assistance for People Living with HIV
records.organization: City of El Paso Department of Public Health
records.description_en: Housing help for eligible people living with HIV.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For eligible people living with HIV in El Paso.
records.notes: Confirmed on City of El Paso 'El Paso Helps' housing page only.

records.name: City of El Paso Community and Human Development - Housing Resources
records.organization: City of El Paso Department of Community and Human Development
records.description_en: City office that funds homeless and housing programs, first-time homebuyer help, and home repair (rehabilitation) for low-income homeowners.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income City of El Paso residents. Rules differ by program.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 212-0138 or visit 300 N. Campbell.
records.notes: Refers residents to El Paso Helps (elpasohelps.org) for crisis support. City general line 311 or (915) 212-0000.
